outlook72h: Indonesia earthquake zone: Aftershocks and landslide risk may continue to affect access and shelter conditions; prioritize contingency shelter and mobile health support. China flood-affected areas (Guangxi): High residual flood and infrastructure failure risks warrant continued monitoring of dam safety and downstream communities. Midwestern U.S.: Receding waters will reveal additional damage; expect ongoing sheltering needs and debris management, with localized flash flood potential where soils remain saturated. British Columbia wildfires: Evacuation patterns may fluctuate with wind shifts and heat; anticipate air quality impacts and intermittent power restoration challenges. Japan/South Korea: Saturated soils sustain elevated landslide risk; transport disruption and localized outage recovery likely to continue. Humanitarian pipelines: IFRC operations (Africa, Myanmar) likely to scale as access improves and assessment data clarifies needs.
regionalTrends: Asia: Concurrent quake and hydro-meteorological crises (Indonesia, China, Japan, South Korea) are straining SAR capacity, shelter, and transport systems.
North America: Flooding (Indiana) and wildfires (British Columbia, U.S. Northwest) are driving prolonged displacement and infrastructure repair backlogs.
Africa: New Red Cross flood operations (Cameroon, Sierra Leone) suggest early-season escalation; situational detail remains limited pending assessments.
Europe: Regional wildfire conditions continue under wind and heat, with Croatia among the hardest hit and cross-border evacuations reported.
